limitations: The v0.1 lab uses ActiveRecord with SQLite; production database-specific behavior still requires deployment-specific evidence.
Static reachability is not runtime execution proof.

Rails assessment and Assurance Graph construction are composed through framework plugins; the shared Inspector/graph cores remain framework-neutral and the default CLI registers the Rails plugin at the composition boundary.

The current graph source scanner is limited to Ruby and Python inputs; this does not restrict the framework identity contract but additional source languages require a separate scanner extension boundary.

ActionCable v0.1 support covers direct public channel actions, direct subscribed/unsubscribed lifecycle callbacks, the conventional ApplicationCable::Connection connect/disconnect lifecycle, unambiguous inherited public RPC actions, direct ActiveSupport::Concern-provided public RPC actions, and inherited/concern-provided subscribed/unsubscribed lifecycle callbacks.

Explicit fully-qualified channel superclass chains are supported; Ruby lexical constant lookup, concern dependencies, ambiguous concern method overlap, custom connection-class resolution, and dynamic channel composition are not statically proven.
Lifecycle callbacks are framework-dispatched and may be non-public Ruby methods; RPC action exposure still requires public visibility.

reject_unauthorized_connection is recognized as connection-local authorization evidence, but authorization in ActionCable connect or subscribed is not projected onto later RPC actions without a stronger stateful proof.
No Rails production runtime corroboration profile is implemented in v0.1.

special_cases.semantics: Publisher wake-up runs only after the outer transaction commits; it is not the durable delivery record.
